title: 45-Day RDN Study Plan
full_3_hour_simulations: optional only when agreed and available

days.focus: Core Principles and an Initial Baseline
days.method: Study food labels, communication, and interpretation of evidence. Complete the Day 1 practice and rate your confidence before reviewing answers.
days.review_checkpoint: Record correct answers and questions without labeling weaknesses from ten items.

days.method: Review assessment, diagnosis/PES, intervention, and monitoring. Explain which information supports each decision. Complete the Day 2 practice.
days.review_checkpoint: Recall two rules from Day 1 without looking.

days.method: Practice units, delivered energy, volume, rate, adequacy, and percentage weight loss. Complete the Day 3 practice.
days.review_checkpoint: Check each calculation with an estimate and the inverse operation.

days.method: Distinguish automatic rules from case-based decisions; identify the plan, barrier, and indicator. Complete the Day 4 practice.
days.review_checkpoint: Review errors from Days 1 and 3; write a case with one detail changed.

days.method: Review FTEs, productivity, budgets, and break-even analysis; distinguish revenue from profit. Complete the Day 5 practice.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Day 2 and check units in management calculations.

days.method: Review yield, portions, production processes, and risk control, identifying the relevant edition of the standard. Complete the Day 6 practice.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Day 3; do not use appearance or odor as proof of safety.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes reviewing six errors or guesses, creating two calculation variations, and summarizing each domain. No new questions are required.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 1: assess whether the routine is workable, identify unfinished topics, and choose three priorities. This is not a pass prediction.

weeks.title: Week 2 | Clinical Assessment and Basic Decisions

days.method: Distinguish screening from assessment; review anthropometrics, intake, laboratory results, and context. Apply these to incomplete cases.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Day 1 and test two earlier rules with new variations.

days.method: Distinguish nutrition from medical diagnoses; identify a modifiable etiology, signs and symptoms, and the first action.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 2 and 8; explain why a distractor does not address the case.

days.method: Compare nutrition needs, feeding, and assessment across the lifespan without extrapolating recommendations between cases.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 3 and 9; consult official references for tested values.

days.method: Study research designs, measures, table interpretation, education, and counseling.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 4 and 8; distinguish association, intervention, and causation.

days.method: Study goals, information that guides MNT, and monitoring; apply them to cases with competing priorities.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 5 and 9; identify the evidence that changes the intervention.

days.method: Review management functions, delegation, training, productivity, and process improvement.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 6 and 10; complete a reviewed mixed set of 20–25 questions if time permits.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes reviewing causes of errors and adjusting the following week. Avoid a question marathon.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 2: use only new or revised items as a measure; small samples remain provisional.

weeks.title: Week 3 | Applied MNT and Food Systems

days.method: Relate stage or treatment to clinical data and individual needs; avoid universal restrictions without context.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 1, 8, and 12; identify the decisive information.

days.method: Study MNT for gastrointestinal conditions, intolerances, and allergies; distinguish etiology from mechanism.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 2, 9, and 13; contrast two similar cases.

days.method: Study indications, routes, composition, calculations, administration, and monitoring. Use supplied targets or an identified clinical source.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 3 and 10; redo calculations without looking at the solutions.

days.method: Review assessment, risk, priorities, progress, and safety in clinical cases; distinguish an isolated sign from a diagnosis.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 4, 11, and 15; avoid drawing broad conclusions from one indicator.

days.method: Study standardized recipes, forecasting, inventory, yield, production systems, and menu adequacy.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 5, 12, and 16; alternate qualitative and numerical problems.

days.method: Review time and temperature, contamination, allergens, HACCP, equipment, and workflow. Identify the rule’s edition and jurisdiction.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 6, 13, and 17; complete a reviewed mixed set of 20–25 questions if possible.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes updating the exam outline checklist, recalling errors, and identifying topics not yet studied.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 3: coverage is not mastery; distinguish topics seen, applied correctly, and still pending.

days.method: Study needs assessment, programs, resources, policy, and outcome indicators.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 8, 15, and 18; distinguish referral from guaranteed eligibility.

days.method: Study learning objectives, methods, readiness, communication, and evaluation of interventions.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 9, 16, and 19; use teach-back and justify the chosen method.

days.method: Study budgets, costs, pricing, service analysis, and target audiences; combine calculations with management decisions.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 10, 17, and 20; distinguish contribution from profit.

days.method: Review ingredient functions, preparation, composition, nutrient retention, and basic physiology.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 11, 18, and 22; study causal relationships rather than lists without context.

days.method: Review scope, responsibility, privacy, documentation, quality, and requirements relevant to the exam outline.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 12, 19, and 23; distinguish technical guidance from local legal rules.

days.method: Cover topics not yet studied. Complete 25–35 reviewed mixed questions in up to 45 minutes; use the remaining time to review answers and record unfinished work.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 13, 20, and 24; do not increase volume if answer review is incomplete.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes consolidating notes and ranking the two priority gaps by exam weight and persistence.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 4: complete the first pass through the outline or identify outstanding areas; adapt Days 29–31.

days.method: Use targeted theory, explain it without notes, and answer new questions on the highest-impact subtopic. Retain a small sample from the other domains.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 15, 22, and 25; distinguish genuine improvement from recognition.

days.method: Repeat the cycle for the second gap; contrast the correct answer with the most attractive distractor.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 16, 23, and 26; look for recurring causes of error.

days.method: Try new variations of calculations and earlier cases; avoid practicing only one topic at a time.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 17, 24, and 27; check whether knowledge transfers to a new question.

days.method: Standard option: 50 minutes of mixed questions without going back, followed by 40 minutes of review. Optional alternative: reserve three uninterrupted hours for up to 145 items.
days.review_checkpoint: The three-hour option requires agreed availability; it is not an existing commitment or a real CAT exam.

days.method: Review errors, guesses, and slow decisions; study the cause rather than memorizing letters. If much remains unfinished, continue reviewing before starting another test.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 19, 26, and 29; distinguish knowledge, calculation, and interpretation issues.

days.method: Solve new variations of errors from the practice test; include all domains in the set.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 20, 27, and 30; check whether recurring errors are decreasing.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes assessing fatigue, consistency, timing, and remaining gaps. Do not compensate for delays by overloading the schedule.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 5: readiness requires consistent evidence from new items; short segments do not measure three-hour endurance.

days.method: Choose next steps, interpret tables, and distinguish plausible alternatives. Prefer items with verifiable explanations.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 22, 29, and 32; resolve source conflicts before scoring.

days.focus: Calculations and Priorities Under Time Pressure
days.method: Combine clinical, finance, and production problems; explain units and decisions without relying only on memorized formulas.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 23, 30, and 33; practice pacing without sacrificing accuracy.

days.method: Use the checklist and recent errors to address remaining weak points. Avoid opening an entirely new question bank.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 24, 31, and 34; test recall after a week.

days.method: Repeat the conditions of Practice A with new questions. Use a 90-minute session including review; reserve three uninterrupted hours only if already feasible.
days.review_checkpoint: Compare similar conditions; do not equate percentages from different question banks.

days.method: Work through incorrect and slow reasoning; distinguish content needs from execution issues.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 26 and 33; define small, verifiable actions.

days.method: Apply new variations of the most common errors. Review formulas, units, decision patterns, and disputed sources.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 27, 34, and 38; a memorized item alone is not confirmation.

days.method: Spend 45 minutes consolidating evidence and deciding whether you are ready, nearly ready with gaps, or need more preparation.
days.review_checkpoint: Checkpoint 6: the decision is not automatic; consider coverage, performance on new items, pace, and, where relevant, endurance.

days.method: Choose the 10–15 rules that most helped correct errors. Explain and apply them to a few new cases; avoid a marathon.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 29 and 36; protect sleep and routine instead of accumulating material.

days.method: If the exam is scheduled, review official instructions, identification, and travel; practice using the calculator and interface. If no date is set, consolidate a maintenance plan.
days.review_checkpoint: Review Days 30 and 37; do not assume the old date shown in the app.

days.method: Briefly review essential points, prepare a personal readiness report, and identify next steps. Day 45 is not automatically exam day.
days.review_checkpoint: If important gaps remain, extend the cycle with specific goals; do not promise a pass.
